the Bodhisatta spent countless past lives doing good deeds and making sacrifices to prepare to help all living beings. After leaving his royal life, he first learned deep meditation from two great teachers, but realized it was not the complete answer. He then spent six years starving himself and practicing extreme hardship, only to find that it physically exhausted him without bringing wisdom. Finally, he gave up extreme hardship and tried the balanced Middle Way, which successfully led him to enlightenment as the Buddha.

The Buddha started out as a prince named Siddhartha Gautama who had everything he could ever want. One day, he left his palace, saw people suffering, and decided to leave his rich lifestyle behind to find answers. After meditating under a giant tree, he finally understood how to find peace and became known as the Buddha, which means "the awakened one." He spent the rest of his life teaching people how to be kind, stay calm, and live a good life without getting attached to worldly things.
